notes.summary: Consistent squared-log conventions pass the constant vertical test and an explicit positive-discrepancy model ray. This is a model special case, not the full residual P19.1 theorem.
notes.detailedSummary: Use dd^c=i/(2π), time t=-log|ζ|², full probability entropy and squared-log divisor coefficients. D=cX0 gives the actual ray ct and energy slope c; unsquared time gives 2c. An explicit bounded P1 ray for 0<ε<1 has energy slope -ε²/2 and entropy slope ε, matching its actual deformation-to-the-normal-cone datum. Products retain these formulas in transcendental and nonprojective product classes.
notes.text:
Fix dd^c=i∂∂bar/(2π), t=-log|ζ|², dd^c log|f|²=[div f], normalized Aubin–Mabuchi energy E(0)=0, and full relative entropy of MA probabilities. Compatibility is U+log|f_D|²=O(1). For D=cX0 on the product configuration, U=-c log|ζ|², so u_t=ct and E(u_t)=ct. Since A^(n+1)=X0²=0 and A^n.X0=V, model energy (A+cX0)^(n+1)/((n+1)V)=c. With s=-log|ζ| the actual ray is 2cs. Stokes gives ∫outside dd^c F=(1/2)∂_sF=∂_tF. Thus Own178's combination of squared-log coefficients, unsquared time and unit energy slope is inconsistent; the printed Green–Riesz equation in 1601.07659v2 requires calibration.

For Ric=-dd^c logω^n, the cohomological Mabuchi expression is M=H+T_-Ric+Sbar E. Differentiation verifies its scalar-curvature variation. In dd_L=i/π, v_s=u_{2s}/2 preserves currents and datum; the cohomological expression instead uses H/2 and Ric_coh=-(1/2)dd_L logω^n. Full probability entropy slope in s is twice the squared-log slope.

A nonzero calibration uses P1: x=log|z|², h(x)=log(1+exp x), y=h'(x), g(y)=y log y+(1-y)log(1-y), and h_t=Legendre(g+t(ε-y)_+), u_t=h_t-h. For x_ε=log(ε/(1-ε)), its three regions are h(x+t)-εt, εx-g(ε), and h(x). Values and first derivatives match. Joint convexity gives psh, and the locally C1,1 Hessian has rank at most one, so homogeneous complex MA vanishes. Bounded comparison on each finite annulus identifies an actual weak geodesic from zero, with -εt≤u_t≤0.

The MA derivative is h''(x+t) on the left, zero in the middle and h''(x) on the right, with no interface atom. Thus E'=-∫_0^ε(ε-y)dy=-ε²/2. Writing k=h'', entropy equals εt+2∫_{-∞}^{x_ε}[log(1+exp(q-t))-log(1+exp q)]k(q)dq. Its remainder lies between -2ε log(1+exp x_ε) and zero. Every finite-time entropy is finite and H/t→ε.

Near (0,0), U differs boundedly from ε log(|z|²+|ζ|²). Therefore its actual datum is D=-εE on the blow-up of (z,ζ), including higher divisorial values. Surface intersections give Γ.B'=1-ε, Γ.E=ε and Γ²/2=-ε²/2. The exceptional component has a=1,b=1 and discrepancy one. Consequently MA_NA=(1-ε)δ_triv+εδ_ord0 and H_NA=ε. The paper proves relative Kählerness through a monomial embedding for integer a,b>d, followed by rational approximation and positive combinations of forms for real parameters.

On P1×Y, restricting Perron competitors to curve fibers proves the actual product-ray assertion. MA probabilities tensor with the same Y probability; energy and entropy remain unchanged, as do the normalized model weights. These are specific model examples, not all maximal rays. Complete proofs and external foundation statements appear in P19.1-argument.md and source-application-ledger.json. Verification-output.json records diagnostic arithmetic and numerical checks; for ε=1/3,t=100, computed H/t=0.3320728681081089. Rerun: python verify.py.

notes.summary: Bounded infinite-entropy starting potentials give stationary datum-zero rays with infinite entropy slope. An exponential-floor criterion is also proved on its exact bounded-ray scope.
notes.detailedSummary: A radial probability density with tiny annular spikes has infinite entropy but a bounded Green potential on P1. Its stationary finite-energy weak ray has zero ordinary datum. Separately, a bounded negative ray from zero with an all-exponential integrable fixed psh floor is either zero or has infinite entropy slope and zero total-ray datum. Neither result proves the full maximal equality or arbitrary-ray classification.
notes.text:
Use n1's conventions. In the Fubini–Study probability coordinate y=|z|²/(1+|z|²), let Z=∑j^-2, m_j=1/(2Zj²), ℓ_j=2^-j-4 exp(-j³), and I_j=[1/3+2∑_{i<j}ℓ_i,1/3+2∑_{i<j}ℓ_i+ℓ_j]. These disjoint intervals lie in [1/3,1/2). The density ρ=1/2+∑(m_j/ℓ_j)1_Ij has mass one and infinite entropy: its interval contributions are at least m_j log(m_j/ℓ_j), whose summands grow proportionally to j.

For the squared chordal Green kernel G(z,a)=log(|z-a|²/((1+|z|²)(1+|a|²))), put w=∫G d(ρω). The background half has a finite constant potential. Each spike is angularly uniform at radii in a fixed compact annulus, and its circle mean is log max(|z|²,r²)-log(1+|z|²)-log(1+r²). This is uniformly bounded for all z and those radii. Hence w is bounded. Logarithmic integrability and Fubini give ω+dd^c w=ρω, so w is bounded psh, lies in E1 and has H(w)=∞.

The stationary total potential is bounded, independent of ζ and solves homogeneous MA. Comparison gives the actual weak ray w_t=w. Pullback preserves boundedness on every modification, so all generic total-space coefficients vanish and its ordinary datum is zero. The trivial model has probability δ_triv and entropy zero, whereas H(w_t)/t=∞ and energy slope is zero. Products extend this example by n1. This concerns infinite-entropy starts and does not refute a smooth-start maximal theorem.

On any compact smooth Kähler manifold, suppose an actual bounded weak ray from zero satisfies u_t≤0 and ψ≤u_t for a fixed psh ψ with C_b=∫exp(-bψ)μ0<∞ for every b>0. Energy affinity gives E(u_t)=-ct, c≥0. The supporting inequality gives ∫(-u_t)MA(u_t)≥ct. Probability entropy duality, proved by Jensen, yields H(u_t)≥bct-log C_b. Taking time to infinity separately for each b, then increasing b, proves H/t→∞ when c>0. If c=0, every term in the negative-potential energy sum is nonpositive; its smooth-volume term vanishes, giving u_t=0 almost everywhere and everywhere as a psh representative.

For the datum, U extends psh across the central divisor and every exp(-bU) is locally integrable by Fubini. On a smooth modification, a positive generic coefficient λ would give U∘π≤λ log|w1|²+C. A Jacobian order k would require integrability of |w1|^(-2bλ+2k), impossible for bλ≥k+1. Thus all total-space coefficients vanish. The precise removability and divisor-subtraction inputs are Demailly's 21 June 2012 primary text, Chapter I Theorem 5.24 and Chapter III Section 8 Proposition 8.16; MP 2409.06221v2 Theorem 4.3.8 supplies divisorial determination. Sections 4–5 of the standalone paper contain the complete proofs. No claim that every nonmaximal ray admits such a floor is made.

notes.summary: The normalized blow-up of (x²,y³) refutes the normal-differential positivity step imported into the September special-Fujita proof. It does not refute its discrepancy theorem or Theorem B.
notes.detailedSummary: A generic exceptional chart has x=w³v,y=w²v,v≠0. The differential vanishes along w=0, and adding a pulled-back background form cannot create normal positivity in the residual ideal-norm curvature. The September Proposition 4.1 imports precisely this companion proof. Its algebraic appendix supplies an alternative, but a checked analytic relative-vanishing transport remains missing here.
notes.text:
On P1×P1, glue I=(x²,y³) near a point to the unit ideal off that point. In the blow-up chart with nonzero T=y³/x², put v=T,w=x/y. Since w²=y/v, w is integral. The ring C[w,v,v^-1] is normal, finite and birational over that chart and gives its normalization. Thus x=w³v,y=w²v is a genuine smooth chart near the generic exceptional divisor F={w=0}, with primitive valuation (3,2).

Along F, both normal derivatives vanish: ∂_w x=3w²v and ∂_w y=2wv. The tangential derivatives vanish too, so dp=0. Moreover log(|x|⁴+|y|⁶)=6 log|w|²+log(|v|⁴+|v|⁶). After subtracting 6[F], residual curvature has a positive tangential component but zero normal component. Every pulled-back smooth background form also vanishes on ∂_w there. Increasing its coefficient cannot make the residual form Kähler. A partition weight may be identically one near the point; smooth generator changes and weights composed with (x,y) have the same vanishing mixed normal derivative. The Jacobian determinant is w⁴v, giving relative canonical order four and ideal order six.

The complete primary analytic proof of Proposition 3.1 in Trusiani arXiv:2605.30063v2, 17 August 2026, was inspected. Browser lines 749–758 assert normal differential injectivity and use it to obtain local Kählerness; lines 823–832 cancel a purported nonvanishing residual determinant. The example refutes that assertion. Trusiani arXiv:2609.31089v1, 25 September 2026, Proposition 4.1 explicitly imports the same proof. Evidence is retained in companion-proof.json and supplied-units/unit-01.txt.

This is a counterexample to a proof step, not to ord_F K≤N(ord_F I-ord_F J(I)), special Fujita existence or the known projective results. Boucksom's Appendix A Proposition A.1 was also inspected completely. It uses relative Nadel vanishing and multiplier subadditivity under smooth algebraic characteristic-zero hypotheses. A checked analytic vanishing/generation application or another local analytic proof could repair the chain; neither is supplied here. Section 10 of P19.1-argument.md gives the standalone proof and limitation, with alternative source evidence in companion-appendix-proof.json.

notes.summary: The SNC defect inequality and log-volume exponent are proved with nonreduced multiplicities. Model recovery and actual-ray transfer, including finite-entropy E1 starts, remain conditional on explicit global inputs.
notes.detailedSummary: Exceptional defect coefficients are a+1-m, giving 0≤Δ≤K_relative. Specified canonical-error and fixed-intersection convergence imply ordered strong model convergence and entropy recovery. A common upper maximal ray gives fixed-time d1 convergence without a roof isometry. Smooth entropy approximation of a finite-entropy start and fixed-time Mabuchi lower semicontinuity prove a sufficient upper transfer. The required global recovery and calibrated slope identities are not established.
notes.text:
For a smooth vertical modification p:Y→𝓧 with SNC reduced central boundaries, put C_𝓧=K_𝓧/(X×P1)+B_red-B. Canonical transitivity gives C_Y=p*C_𝓧+Δ, with Δ=K_Y/𝓧+(p*B)_red-p*B_red. Strict transforms have coefficient zero. For an exceptional F, write a=ord_F K_Y/𝓧 and m=ord_F p*B_red≥1. Its coefficient is a+1-m. Pulling back a logarithmic top form for the SNC boundary produces at most one dw1/w1 pole, since repeated such differentials wedge to zero. Hence a-m≥-1 and 0≤Δ≤K_Y/𝓧. Kähler positivity then bounds β_k^n.Δ_k by β_k^n.K_Yk/𝓧. Canonical-error convergence, not volume convergence alone, makes this vanish.

The entropy exponent is independently checked. On an SNC dominating model use F=-∑(a_i+1-b_i)log|z_i|²+O(1). Multiplying exp(F) by pullback total volume gives ∏|z_i|^(2(b_i-1)). With q_i=-log|z_i|² and t=∑b_iq_i, division by base area leaves a simplex slice of size O((1+t)^(r-1)). A finite cover yields ∫exp(F_t)μ0≤C(1+t)^n. The coefficients are nonnegative by log-canonicity of the product pair, so the logarithm of this integral is O(log t). Multiplicities b_i cannot be discarded. A calibrated mixed pairing limit is still needed to derive the full entropy lower bound.

Conditional model recovery assumes actual equivariant SNC vertical data β_k=p_k*Γ-E_k are Kähler, E_k≥0, with three convergences: top volume to Vol Γ, β_k^n.K_Yk/𝓧→0, and β_k^n.p_k*ξ→<Γ^n>.ξ for every fixed smooth real closed (1,1) class ξ. MPWN 2509.09442v1 Propositions 9.1.3 and 9.1.5 state, for f_D≥1 and φ=Pα(f_D), E_NA(φ)=Vol Γ/((n+1)V) and H_NA(φ)=<Γ^n>.C_𝓧/V. Effectivity gives φ_k≤φ; these formulas and the defect bound give energy and entropy convergence. For J(a,b)=E_NA(a)-E_NA(b)+∫(b-a)MA_NA(a), order gives 0≤J(φ,φ_k)≤E_NA(φ)-E_NA(φ_k). MPWN Theorem 5.2.2 then supplies strong convergence after normalization; energy convergence restores the constants. The special-data assumptions are not globally granted, because of n3 and the remaining application audit.

Assume the actual maximal-ray correspondence preserves order in datum and start and satisfies E(r_t^{w,θ})=E(w)+tE_NA(θ). MPWN Lemma 5.0.5 gives fixed-output L1 convergence for weakly convergent NA data with bounded J; its scalar identity requires the correction |a-b|=2(max(a,b)-b)-(a-b). For strong η_j→φ, put λ_j=max(η_j,φ). Supporting inequalities give E_NA(λ_j)→E_NA(φ). Its actual maximal ray is a common upper ray, giving d1(r_t^{w,η_j},r_t^{w,φ})≤t[2E_NA(λ_j)-E_NA(η_j)-E_NA(φ)]→0.

For H(w)<∞, BDL 1510.01260v2 Theorem 3.2 provides smooth w_j with d1 and entropy convergence. Darvas 1409.2072v2 Theorem 5.5 and the supporting inequality give E(max(w_j,w))→E(w); the start-change error is at most 2E(max(w_j,w))-E(w_j)-E(w), independent of time. Assuming strong/entropy model recovery, calibrated model Mabuchi slopes and a finite matching target mixed-energy slope, convexity gives M(r_{j,t})≤M(w_j)+tM_NA(η_j). Fix time first and use BDL Theorem 4.7 lower semicontinuity to obtain M(r_t)≤M(w)+tM_NA(φ). Only then take time to infinity and subtract the matching mixed slope. This proves the conditional limsup entropy upper bound. Sections 6–9 contain complete proofs and precise signatures. It is neither arbitrary strong entropy continuity nor an unconditional maximal equality.
